title: Car Fleet
takeaways: Sorting elements relative to destination simplifies tracking interactions.
Transforming speed and distance into time-to-target reduces a dynamic simulation to static comparisons.
A monotonic stack or maintaining a running maximum time tracks active fleet leaders efficiently.

REFRAME: do not compute WHERE cars meet, compare WHEN they arrive. Car i joins the fleet ahead iff time[i] <= time[ahead], because starting behind and arriving no later means it must have caught up before the target.
Any ratio in a motion/geometry problem must be double. Cast ONE operand before dividing - casting the result is too late, truncation already happened.
Guard before dividing: (cur.speed > p.speed) && (...) prevents both a negative catch-up time and a divide-by-zero on equal speeds.
A problem's topic tag names a POSSIBLE tool, not the necessary one. Car Fleet is tagged Stack, but the stack is only a running maximum in disguise.

ADDITIVE DEBUGGING is the real lesson here: V2 layered the new arrival-time framing ON TOP of the old catch-up geometry instead of replacing it, and came out longer, slower and MORE wrong (46% vs 45% failure). Deleting the geometry - changing nothing else but if->while and <= -> < - passed 30000/30000. When you adopt a new framing, delete the old one first; if both are in the code, at least one is wrong. Ask 'what can I remove?' before 'what can I add?'
Operator precedence: / binds tighter than -, so `target - pos / time` is `target - (pos/time)`. Parenthesise any mixed arithmetic whose grouping matters.

Left-to-right (farthest from target first) is a valid alternative direction: each new car is closer to the target than everything on the stack, so pop every fleet whose arrival time is <= mine, then push.
revisit_reason: STRUGGLED BADLY - took 4 attempts. V1: catch-up geometry with integer division and no guard that the rear car is faster (negative catch-up time meant a SLOWER car appeared to catch the one ahead) - failed LC example 1 and ~45% of random tests. V2: layered the arrival-time reframe ON TOP of the geometry instead of replacing it, plus an operator-precedence bug (`target - pos / time` is `target - (pos/time)`) - 46% failure, WORSE than V1; deleting the added machinery passed 30000/30000. V3: adjacent/pairwise comparison of raw times - failed target=10, position=[0,4,2], speed=[2,1,3]. V4 (passing): sort by position, scan BACKWARD from the target, new fleet only when time > running max. Verified 0/40000. RE-SOLVE COLD: the pass condition is not just correctness but reaching V4 directly, and collapsing the stack to a single scalar (it is a running max in disguise - O(1) space).
self_assessment: Four attempts. The blocker was conceptual, not syntactic: times[i] is a car's arrival time ONLY IF the road ahead is empty. Once a car joins a fleet its real arrival becomes the fleet's, and that must propagate backward - which is exactly what a running max does and what pairwise comparison cannot do. Also hand-traced the killer case wrong by tracing the arithmetic instead of the physics; a position-vs-time table settled it in four rows.
